title: Momentum Accelerator: 90-day one-pager + all-hands brief
body:
Purpose

This is a compact, action-oriented 90-day "Momentum Accelerator" one-pager intended to:
- Align leadership and ICs on a narrow set of company-wide priorities for the quarter
- Provide a short, crowd-friendly all-hands slot and exec update script
- Surface clear owner/next-step list and escalation paths for blockers

Audience: Execs, engineering heads, product leads, people ops, marketing. Pre-read required for execs and managers.

Why this exists (context)
- We’ve accumulated a long backlog of cross-team dependencies that slows rollouts and degrades unit economics.
- Need a single, lightweight cadence to force decisions, reduce rework, and reallocate focus toward production-readiness metrics.
- This doc is intentionally narrow: 3 company OKRs + one operational risk focus for the quarter.

90-day focus (top-level)
- Time window: Nov 10 — Feb 9 (12 weeks)
- Guiding principle: Reduce mean inference unit cost and tail latency while increasing customer-facing uptime.

Draft company OKRs (candidate)
1) OKR 1 — Improve production unit economics
   - Objective: Reduce per-token cost for hosted API by 18% while maintaining quality SLOs.
   - Key results:
     * K1.1: Decrease average tokens-per-request compute cost by 10% through batching/quantization guidance (owner: Platform Product — Ravi S.).
     * K1.2: Deploy two recommended quantization profiles across top-5 models (owner: Serving Runtime — Marcus L.).
     * K1.3: Ship an automated suggestion engine in Optimize for 80% of customers on medium workloads (owner: Optimize PM — Nina G.).

2) OKR 2 — Harden reliability across environments
   - Objective: Bring P95 latency SLA compliance to 99.5% for Dedicated customers.
   - Key results:
     * K2.1: Implement degraded-mode fallback routing for cross-region capacity shortages (owner: Infra SRE — Eleanor P.).
     * K2.2: Add synthetic blackbox tests that exercise KV cache reuse at 4x sequence lengths (owner: Observability Eng — Marcus L.).
     * K2.3: Reduce mean time to fallback by 40% (target MTBF reduction tracked in SLO board) (owner: SRE Lead — Ravi S.).

3) OKR 3 — Launch an enterprise-ready private on-prem quickstart
   - Objective: Deliver a hardened Private quickstart path for regulated customers, reducing onboarding time by 50%.
   - Key results:
     * K3.1: Publish a VPC deployment template and installer with KMS integration (owner: Private Deployments PM — Nina G.).
     * K3.2: Run two pilot customers and capture 10 onboarding issues and mitigations (owner: Solutions Eng — Eleanor P.).
     * K3.3: Add audit-log collection to the console for retention periods (owner: Console Product — Avery C.).

Operational risk focus (quarterly): Cross-team release choke points
- Symptom: Features are blocked at staging due to inconsistent compatibility specs between runtime and infra (model variants, kernel sets).
- Mitigations:
  * Weekly triage between serving-runtime, infra, and release-engineering on release tickets tagged "release-choke".
  * Mandatory prerelease checklist item: "compatibility smoke" that gates canary promotion.
  * Point-person escalation: Marcus L. -> Ravi S. -> CTO (if >48h unresolved).

All-hands slot (15 minutes) — run-of-show (short & execution oriented)\- 0:00-01:30 — Quick framing (CEO) — Why we’re doing Momentum Accelerator (one slide, one sentence mission link)
- 01:30-06:00 — Exec update highlights (VP Eng, VP Product) — bullets only (metrics vs baseline)
- 06:00-10:00 — Tactical calls-to-action (three items): cost playbook, reliability triage, private quickstart pilot signup (assign owners + sign-up URL)
- 10:00-13:00 — Live demo (30s) or screenshot of Optimize suggestion engine (if shipped)
- 13:00-15:00 — Q&A + explicit next-step ask (managers do 1:1 sync w/teams within 48h)

Pre-read for all-hands (to be uploaded 48h before):
- One-page OKR summary (this doc)
- Links to two short tickets: ACCEL-12 (cost playbook rollout), ACCEL-34 (private quickstart pilot intake)

Exec update talking points (one-liners to use)
- "We’ve selected three outcomes this quarter: cost, reliability, and private onboarding. These are tightly scoped with owners and measurable KRs."
- "Immediate action: managers should allocate 10% of sprint capacity to instrumentation and smoke testing for their top impacted routes."
- "If a release becomes blocked for >48 hours, escalate to the on-call owner and tag the ticket release-choke; leadership will intervene."

Communication plan (high level)
- Week 0 (today): Publish this one-pager to Drive, ping leaders in #leadership.
- Week 1: All-hands slot + post-handoff thread with owners and tickets.
- Week 3: Midpoint check-in (30m sync with execs + writeup).
- Week 6: Early telemetry readout — share dashboard snapshot + red/amber/green signal per OKR.
- Week 12: Final readout in an all-company memo + short exec debrief.

Roles / RACI (compact)
- Responsible: Owners listed alongside each KR (Ravi, Marcus, Nina, Eleanor, Avery).
- Accountable: CTO for execution; CEO for prioritization.
- Consulted: Solutions Eng, Release Eng, Sales engineering.
- Informed: All engineers, product managers, CS managers.

Decision heuristics (for triage)
- If a fix improves cost by >5% but has >3% regression in quality metric, escalate and require cross-team mitigation plan.
- Prioritize changes that unblock >2 customers or reduce fleet spend >$20k/month.

Known unknowns / open questions
- Quantization profiles: which vendor libs do we standardize on? (svc: open item for Serving Runtime).
- Onboarding metric definition: what counts as "reduced onboarding time" for Private? (ops: define in pilot intake).
- Resource trade-offs: how should teams deprioritize mid-quarter if a P0 customer needs emergency work? (policy ask for execs).

Quick TODOs (next 7 days)
- [ ] Finalize OKR language and publish to Confluence (owner: Avery C., due: Nov 12).
- [ ] Create ACCEL epic and tag top-10 tickets (owner: Release Eng triage — Marcus L., due: Nov 13).
- [ ] Prepare slide for All-hands and confirm demo slot (owner: CEO office — Nina G., due: Nov 14).

Escalation ladder (practical)
- Level 1: Owner handles via ticket and hands to triage channel (#accel-triage).
- Level 2: If unresolved 24h, alert SRE lead and platform PM.
- Level 3: If unresolved 48h with customer impact, escalate to CTO/CEO.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the all-hands message short; people remember 2-3 concrete asks.
- Don’t over-commit to KR %s until we confirm baseline telemetry.
- We need a simple dashboard card for each KR in the Console — raise ticket to Console product.

Appendix: Suggested artifact links (for pre-read)
- Cost playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ACCEL-90
- ACCEL epic: ACCEL-12
- Optimize PR for suggestion engine: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345

Revision history:

- v0.2 (2025-11-09) added OKR KRs and owners (collabs: Nina, Marcus)
- v0.3 (2025-11-12) added all-hands run-of-show + escalation ladder (in review)

End of doc.
